metadata.geoclick:note: Shared style for all admin-1 demo maps. The 'targets' source url is a placeholder (pmtiles://./tiles.pmtiles) — the map viewer composes the final style per map by replacing it with that map's own tiles.pmtiles URL. Each tileset has two source-layers (see data/scripts/build-map.ts): 'targets' (polygons, for fill/outline/hit-testing) and 'labels' (one point per feature at its precomputed centroid). This style deliberately does not render a name label layer: Geoclick is a place-recognition game, so showing region names on the map by default would give away the answer. The 'labels' source-layer still exists in the tiles for the app to use on demand (e.g. a per-click popup, a guided tour reveal, or a solved quiz target), just not as an always-on style layer or even a MapLibre symbol layer — a DOM-based maplibregl.Popup per solved/revealed target turned out more reliable than driving a symbol layer's opacity from feature-state, which hit MapLibre's collision/placement system hiding labels unpredictably even with text-allow-overlap+text-ignore-placement set (see QuizView.svelte). promoteId 'name' lets the app call setFeatureState by target name directly (map.json's Target.name), without needing to query the source for a feature first — safe because target names are unique within a single map. Feature-states used across views: 'highlighted' (explore click, tour reveal), 'quizHover' (drag-to-match, region under the dragged slip), 'quizCorrect' (drag-to-match, region solved), 'quizRevealed' (drag-to-match, auto-solved after too many wrong attempts — distinct muted color, doesn't count as a real success), 'quizWrong' (drag-to-match, brief flash on whichever region was actually — wrongly — dropped on; takes priority over every other state since it's a transient overlay that can land on an already-solved region if a different slip gets dropped there by mistake).
